summary: FIX-1's genuinely-fixed original defect (NOISE_DISCOUNTED laundering unrelated noise adjacency into acceptance) stays closed - not reopened by any construction tried. But titleBodySeparationHolds's entire discriminating power rests on one unstated assumption: 'a fake in-text citation's continuation is lowercase; a real heading's own body is not.' That assumption is false whenever an in-text citation is itself a grammatically ordinary, well-punctuated sentence followed by a new sentence - which in real drafting is capitalized (or digit-led), exactly like a real heading's own body. Every such construction still launders a citation into a false top-level SECTION/ARTICLE and reproduces the module's own named 'rank-stack corruption' failure class (a real child clause silently re-parented to the spurious node) - with ZERO footnote, ZERO page-number noise, ZERO run-on lowercase grammar, and in several cases ZERO whitespace irregularity of any kind. The new wrap-tolerance mechanism adds its own narrower, additional false-positive path on top of this: identical text, merely re-wrapped across a line break immediately before its own tell-tale lowercase continuation, flips a correct rejection into a false acceptance (a minimal, mechanistic before/after pair, not merely a hypothetical). A real-world 'Term. means ...' definitions-section drafting convention is also wrongly vetoed as a false negative, silently merging its real content into the preceding section's owned span.

falsifications.test: 2. FALSIFICATION > citation followed by a completely ordinary capitalized new sentence
falsifications.construction:
Section 6.08 Restricted Payments. The Borrower shall not make any Restricted Payment except as otherwise agreed.
Section 6.09 Limitation on Restricted Payments. This citation refers to a limitation described in the Credit Agreement and does not itself constitute an independent covenant of this Agreement.
(a) Permitted Liens existing on the Closing Date.

Section 6.10 Liens. ...
falsifications.expected: 6.09 is not a real heading; clause (a) belongs to 6.08.
falsifications.actual: 6.09 is accepted as a top-level SECTION; clause (a) is re-parented to 6.09.
falsifications.whyItMatters: No footnote, no page-number noise, no lowercase run-on, no unusual whitespace - just an ordinary citation ending its own sentence with a real period, followed by an ordinary new sentence. This is not an edge case; it is the default shape of a well-written in-text citation, and it reproduces the exact rank-stack corruption the fix was certified to close.

falsifications.test: 2. FALSIFICATION > citation followed by a quoted defined term
falsifications.whyItMatters: Confirms the same gap for the opening-quote self-contained-start branch, independently of the plain-capital-letter branch.

falsifications.test: 2. FALSIFICATION > citation followed by ALL-CAPS defined-term acronym (GAAP)
falsifications.whyItMatters: An ALL-CAPS acronym starting the next sentence is exactly as common in real drafting as a Title-Case sentence start, and defeats the signal identically.

falsifications.test: 2. FALSIFICATION > citation followed by a digit-led ordinary sentence (50% ...)
falsifications.whyItMatters: A leading digit is treated identically to an uppercase letter by looksLikeNewContentStart - an ordinary numeric sentence opener (a percentage, a dollar figure, a defined threshold) is just as common in contracts as a capitalized one.

falsifications.test: 2. FALSIFICATION > two genuinely unrelated short lines wrapped together
falsifications.actual: A citation fragment ('Waiver of') glued via a line wrap to a wholly unrelated sentence about notice delivery is accepted as 'Section 9.05'.
falsifications.whyItMatters: Directly exercises the task's named 'two different unrelated short lines that happen to look wrapped into one heading-shaped span' risk.

falsifications.test: 3. FALSIFICATION > Case C vs Case D
falsifications.construction: Identical text in both cases (the classic lowercase-run-on false citation, 'Limitation on Restricted Payments. is only a cross-reference...'). Case C: no line wrap. Case D: one newline inserted between 'Limitation on' and 'Restricted Payments.'
falsifications.expected: Both cases reject 3.09 identically - a line-wrap position is a PDF-extraction artifact, never real evidence.
falsifications.actual: Case C correctly rejects 3.09 (clause (a) stays parented to 3.08). Case D - the SAME text, re-wrapped - wrongly ACCEPTS 3.09 and re-parents clause (a) to it.
falsifications.whyItMatters: This is the sharpest, most mechanistic falsification in the matrix: it isolates the wrap-tolerance mechanism specifically (looksLikeNewContentStartAfterPossibleTitleWrap's plain-check-first, short-window behavior) as the causal factor, independent of the general capitalization gap in F1-F5. The wrap-tolerance mechanism was added to rescue REAL wrapped titles (DSGR ARTICLE III, CONMED SECTION 2.10/2.4) but, as built, also rescues a FAKE wrapped citation whenever the wrap happens to land before its own tell-tale lowercase word - which is exactly the scrutiny this audit's brief asked for ('a mechanism built to fix a real-fixture regression could itself introduce a new false-positive path').

falsifications.construction: Section 1.08 Applicable Margin. means, with respect to any Loan, the percentage per annum set forth in the Pricing Grid...
falsifications.actual: 1.08 is dropped entirely (titleBodySeparationHolds vetoes it, since 'means' is lowercase); its real text is silently absorbed into 1.07's owned span (charEnd(1.07) === charStart(1.09)).
falsifications.severity: secondary - lower confidence than F1-F9 since this exact convention was not found in any of the four certified real fixtures (FWRG/LSB/CONMED/DSGR), so it does not contradict the implementer's own fixture-scoped claim. Reported because 'Term. means ...' (omitting a repeated defined-term subject) is a real, common drafting convention outside this specific fixture set, and the resulting data corruption (one section's real text silently attributed to a different section) is the same class of harm rank-stack corruption protects against, just in the false-negative direction.

residualRiskFromImplementerReportRevisit.auditorFinding: This significantly understates the risk. The gap is not confined to the wrap-tolerance bound at all (F1-F5, F9 need no wrap-tolerance whatsoever - the PLAIN, non-wrap check is what's fooled), is not coincidental (it fires on the single most common real-world citation shape: a citation that is its own complete, well-punctuated sentence), and is trivially reproducible without any adversarial cleverness.

recommendation: Do not close FIX-1 as CERTIFIED_CLOSED. The fix correctly closes the specific NOISE_DISCOUNTED defect and the specific lowercase-run-on shape the required matrix tests, but titleBodySeparationHolds needs a materially different design (or an explicit, documented scope narrowing to 'only catches lowercase-run-on citations, not well-punctuated ones') before the false-heading class can be considered closed. The wrap-tolerance mechanism in particular should not treat a bare capital-letter/digit/keyword check as sufficient at the FIRST character after a resumption point without also verifying the resumed text does not itself trail off into an ordinary sentence shortly after - the same failure this file's own doc-comment says an early open-ended/multi-hop draft was rejected for reintroducing, just reached from the opposite (too-short-a-check) direction instead of a too-long one.
